title: Construction of the canonical formal glueing functor
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring map, $t\in\mathbf N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$. In the category of formal glueing data [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] there exists a functor $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ with $\mathrm{Can}(M)=(S\otimes_R M,(M_{f_i})_i,(c^M_{f_i})_i,(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$ on every object and $\mathrm{Can}(h)=(1\otimes h,(h_{f_i})_i)$ on every linear map. The object components are equal as bundled modules, and structural maps and morphism components are the actual canonical maps, identified by heterogeneous equality after these equalities. No flatness or quotient hypothesis is assumed. Base change and localizations have the meanings in [def-weil-module-base-change] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

proof.text: Apply exists_canonical_functor_objects separately to each module. Choose these objects; the bundled module equalities and heterogeneous equalities fix all data fields (linear equivalences are determined by their forward maps), while the remaining fields are proofs. This gives an object assignment with its required properties.

Apply canonical_functor_maps to this object assignment. Package the supplied morphism assignment, identity law and composition law as a CategoryTheory.Functor into Data. The object and map specifications are precisely the original conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_canonical_functor {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R) :
    ∃ Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f,
      (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))) ∧
      (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (Can.map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom))
